structure.overview: The case concerns Applicants challenging the Refugee Appeal Division's (RAD) analysis under the second prong of the Internal Flight Alternative (IFA) test regarding persecution risk as pro-Khalistan supporters. The Applicants argue RAD failed to properly consider their political beliefs and the risk of inability to express those beliefs in India, while the Respondent defends RAD's decision as reasonable. The Federal Court dismissed the judicial review, finding RAD's decision reasonably addressed the Applicants' political beliefs and risk of persecution in the IFA context.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: RPD found Applicants failed to prove Punjab police had means or motivation to track them outside Punjab; Principal Applicant lacked public profile attracting Indian authorities' attention.

summaries.speaker: below

citations.why: RAD relied on this case to support motivation analysis in IFA test

summaries.speaker: below

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court explains reasonableness standard requires justification, transparency, intelligibility; misapprehension of evidence may render decision unreasonable; burden on challenger, citing Vavilov.

citations.why: Defines reasonableness criteria and burden on challenger

summaries.summary: Second prong requires actual evidence of jeopardy in IFA; applicant must prove IFA not viable; cites Olusola 2020 FC 799 and others.
